_readme: Field help for the Opportunity form and its guided flow (form kit P4.3; see form_kit/field_help.py). hint: the short line under the field, which is also the field's description. help: the longer (i) explanation. Changed by PR. article: the Knowledge Article the Learn more links open, each field at its step's anchor.

custom_opportunity_summary.hint: One plain-English line answering "what is this?" - e.g. "Sapphire hardware access + VNC for controller". Written by the Account Executive; the detail lives in Scope, not here.

custom_lead_source.hint: Where this opportunity came from. Mirrors Customer.custom_lead_source and Lead.custom_lead_source.

custom_probability_by_hand.hint: Ticked when someone types the probability: a stage change then keeps it. Untick to go back to the stage's default (Sales Activity Settings).

custom_design_customer_requests.hint: The customer's ask, in their own words - entered by Sales when the request comes in. Don't break it down here; one row per ask (or everything in one row) is fine.

custom_design_deliverables.hint: The internal breakdown of what we'll deliver - translated from the Customer Requests by the PM/design team (PRO-0204 Step 6). Not filled in by Sales.

custom_build_customer_requests.hint: The customer's ask, in their own words - entered by Sales when the request comes in. Don't break it down here; one row per ask (or everything in one row) is fine.

custom_build_deliverables.hint: The internal breakdown of what we'll deliver - translated from the Customer Requests by the PM/design team (PRO-0204 Step 6). Not filled in by Sales.

custom_service_customer_requests.hint: The customer's ask, in their own words - entered by Sales when the request comes in. Don't break it down here; one row per ask (or everything in one row) is fine.

custom_service_deliverables.hint: The internal breakdown of what we'll deliver - translated from the Customer Requests by the PM/design team (PRO-0204 Step 6). Not filled in by Sales.

custom_rent_customer_requests.hint: The customer's ask, in their own words - entered by Sales when the request comes in. Don't break it down here; one row per ask (or everything in one row) is fine.

custom_rent_deliverables.hint: The internal breakdown of what we'll deliver - translated from the Customer Requests by the PM/design team (PRO-0204 Step 6). Not filled in by Sales.

custom_first_invoice_percentage.hint: How much of the project amount goes on the first invoice to the customer. Named in the hand-off note to Billing (Hand-Off Process step 4), together with the money it works out to. Blank means the note asks Billing to confirm the amount with Sales rather than inventing one.

custom_billing_email.hint: Where the hand-off note for step 4 (Create Accounting Project & Send Invoice) is addressed. Leave blank for the configured Billing route (billing@sapphirefountains.com) — this is an override, not a required setting, and several addresses may be separated by commas.

custom_stage_changed_on.hint: Timestamp of the last status change - feeds the days-in-stage aging on the Sales Pipeline board.

custom_utm_source.hint: Raw utm_source from the landing URL. NOT erpnext's own utm_source, which is a Link to the empty UTM Source taxonomy and is reserved for the fountain-move stray-Contact suppression. See crm_enhancements/attribution.py.

custom_utm_medium.hint: Raw utm_medium. Drives the derived Lead Source: cpc/ppc -> Advertisement, email -> Email Campaign, social -> Social Media Campaign.

custom_utm_campaign.hint: Raw utm_campaign. Data, not a Link, so an arbitrary campaign slug cannot spawn junk taxonomy rows.

custom_utm_id.hint: Raw utm_id -- the ad platform's own campaign ID, written by its dynamic URL macro (Google ValueTrack campaignid, Meta campaign.id, LinkedIn CAMPAIGN_ID). Equals Ad Campaign.external_id: the spend-to-lead join key (TASK-2026-01570).

custom_utm_content.hint: Raw utm_content -- which creative or placement was clicked.

custom_utm_term.hint: Raw utm_term -- the paid keyword. erpnext ships no equivalent field.

custom_gclid.hint: Google Ads click identifier. Auto-tagging sets it even when no utm_* parameters are present, so it is checked first when deriving a Lead Source.

custom_landing_page.hint: First page of the session on the marketing site. Small Text because a query-string-bearing URL overflows Data(140).

custom_first_referrer.hint: document.referrer at session entry. Distinguishes organic search from a direct visit when utm parameters are absent.

custom_attribution_captured_on.hint: Stamped once, when attribution first landed on this record. Read-only: derived, and a hand-edit would misdate the acquisition.

custom_handoff_meeting_held.hint: Set by the Hand-Off Meeting buttons only. Until this is ticked (or the hand-off is skipped with a reason), no Project can be created from this Opportunity.

custom_handoff_meeting_on.hint: Server-generated. Carried onto the Project's step 2 row.

custom_handoff_meeting_by.hint: Server-generated. Carried onto the Project's step 2 row.

custom_handoff_event.hint: The calendar Event created by the “Hold Hand-Off Meeting” button.

custom_handoff_skip_reason.hint: Why the hand-off meeting was skipped. Recorded by a System Manager through the permission-gated skip action, and copied onto the Project's step 2 row with a [SKIPPED] prefix.

custom_handoff_due_by.hint: Two business days from the Opportunity being marked Closed Won. Stamped once, at the transition.

custom_launch_deadline.hint: Seven business days from Closed Won — the meeting's headline goal for holding the Project Launch Meeting (step 7). Stamped once, at the transition.

custom_handoff_gate_applies.hint: Set only on a genuine transition into Closed Won, so the pre-existing Closed Won backlog stays exempt from the hand-off gate. Do not set by hand.
